content: 1. Ovarian enlargement and hyperstimulation can occur as a result of treatment. 2. Arterial thromboembolism, though rare, is a potentially fatal complication. 3. Gynecomastia (enlargement of breast tissue) may develop in males. 4. Hemoperitoneum, or the presence of blood in the peritoneal cavity, is a possible adverse event. 5. This medication may cause harm to a developing fetus if used during pregnancy. 6. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. 7. Elevated levels of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) may indicate primary ovarian failure. 8. The presence of uncontrolled non-gonadal endocrinopathies, such as thyroid, adrenal, or pituitary disorders, is a contraindication for use. 9. Sex hormone-dependent tumors of the reproductive tract and accessory organs are contraindications for this treatment. 10. Tumors of the pituitary gland or hypothalamus are also contraindications. 11. Abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin should be evaluated before initiating therapy. 12. Ovarian cysts or unexplained ovarian enlargement not due to polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) require further investigation before treatment. 13. This medication should only be administered by physicians with extensive experience in managing fertility disorders. 14. Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) has been reported and is distinct from uncomplicated ovarian enlargement. OHSS can progress rapidly and is characterized by increased vascular permeability, leading to fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity, thorax, and potentially the pericardium. 15. To minimize the risk of abnormal ovarian enlargement, the lowest effective dose should be used. If the ovaries are enlarged on the last day of therapy, human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) should not be administered due to the risk of OHSS. 16. Pulmonary and vascular complications, such as atelectasis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), may occur. 17. Ovarian torsion has been reported following gonadotropin treatment. 18. Multi-fetal gestation and births are possible outcomes of gonadotropin therapy. 19. The incidence of congenital malformations may be slightly higher following assisted reproductive technologies (ART), such as in vitro fertilization (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), likely due to parental characteristics. 20. Women undergoing ART, particularly those with tubal abnormalities, may have an increased risk of ectopic pregnancy. 21. An increased incidence of spontaneous abortion and ovarian neoplasms has been observed, though causality has not been established. 22. This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category X and must not be used during pregnancy. 23. It is unknown whether this drug is excreted in breast milk; caution is advised during lactation. 24. Headache, mild abdominal pain or bloating, redness or pain at the injection site, breast tenderness, and dizziness are common side effects. 25. This medication may cause dizziness, and alcohol or cannabis use can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you are sure you can do so safely. 26. Multiple births may occur as a result of this treatment. 27. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for instructions. 28. Store the medication in the refrigerator or at room temperature, protected from light. Do not freeze. 29. Properly discard the medication when it is expired or no longer needed. 30. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your healthcare provider. 31. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. 32. Routine blood hormone tests (e.g., estradiol levels) and vaginal ultrasounds should be performed during treatment to monitor response and safety. 33. Lifestyle changes, such as limiting alcohol consumption and quitting smoking, may enhance the effectiveness of this medication.
